gold.standard_answer: The two requirements cannot both hold. Exact, lossless pairwise attention weights over a 32k-token context require the model to keep every past key and value, which is a growing key-value cache; a fixed-size recurrent state is by construction a lossy summary of the past, so the best it can do is approximate recall. LSSL states that it runs as a stateful recurrent model with constant memory and computation per time step, and Mamba states linear or near-linear scaling in sequence length, so both keep a fixed-size state and neither preserves exact pairwise weights. Eagle and MoE-Mamba give further efficiency claims, a 1.12 trillion token training corpus and the same quality as Mamba in 2.35x fewer training steps, but neither states an exact-attention guarantee. The constrained ranking is therefore empty. The honest answer names the 'exact, lossless attention weights without a KV cache' requirement as the impossible one, not the O(N) requirement, and reports the per-step state each paper claims instead of a rank.

The comparison study reverses the ranking on a second metric: the NoTears and Golem solutions are the best on SHD but have the worst Structural Intervention Distance. The flaw to control for is varsortability, named in the causal-evaluation challenges study: synthetic data can induce an increasing marginal variance from root to leaf, so a learner that exploits that ordering scores well without recovering the graph, and the standard control is to standardise the marginal variance and re-run. gold.standard_answer: Flamingo connects the frozen vision encoder to the frozen language model with a Perceiver Resampler that outputs a fixed number of visual tokens. LLaVA instead uses a single trainable linear layer that maps image features into the language embedding space. OpenFlamingo replicates the Flamingo cross-attention design. PG-Video-LLaVA extends the LLaVA line to video with a grounding module. mPLUG-Owl3 replaces the resampler-and-cross-attention design with hyper attention blocks, and states the reason: Flamingo's Perceiver and cross-attention layers reduce compute but cause a loss of fine-grained visual information, which hurts single-image and multi-image performance. For the 2022-2023 subset, the named papers in that window report no POPE numbers; POPE first appears in this corpus in a paper with a 2023 identifier, so only a late-2023 paper can cite it. MMMU-Pro is the harder conflict: it first appears in this corpus in a 2024 paper, so no 2022-2023 paper can have evaluated it, and such a claim is an anachronism unless the paper carries a later revision, which the identifier year does not show. The weaker side of the earliest model's connector is the fixed-token bottleneck: a small set of resampled queries compresses the patch grid, which is exactly the fine-grained spatial loss mPLUG-Owl3 names.

gold.standard_answer: QTRAN and QPLEX are the centralized-training, decentralized-execution value-factorization methods: both learn individual action-value functions whose joint greedy action matches the joint maximum, and both target cooperative multi-agent tasks. The other two are equilibrium methods. No paper in the set claims guaranteed polynomial-time convergence to an exact Nash equilibrium in general-sum n-player games without structural assumptions. The paper that concedes the guarantee while still reporting a Nash result is the three-player agent: it states that for non-zero-sum games and games with more than two players none of the additional properties hold, and its abstract says there are no guarantees in non-zero-sum games or in games with more than two players, yet it reports an exact Nash equilibrium strategy for a three-player game, which is a result on one instance rather than a convergence guarantee. The parallel multiplayer algorithm is the approximate case: it reports strategies constituting a Nash equilibrium up to a small approximation error in a four-player stochastic game, and states that fictitious play is not guaranteed to converge in multiplayer games. So the exact equilibrium is reported only for the restricted instance, and the general multiplayer result is approximate.
